title: Is private equity setting the stage for technical-materials M&A?
content:
Nonwovenn and CorpAcq launched TMG to acquire specialist-materials businesses across the UK, Europe and North America.
TMG targets engineered textiles, films, composites and laminated products for filtration, thermal management, electrification and PFAS alternatives.
Nonwovenn grew turnover from £19 million in 2016 to £46 million in 2025, with 19 consecutive profitable years.

title: Can India polyester operating rate above 80%, rising feedstock cost?
content:
India's polyester industry is running at more than 80 per cent capacity, with rising crude and PTA costs testing the pace.
Domestic PTA has climbed 7 per cent since September 1 to cross $1,030 per ton; Indian Basket crude touched $128.70 per barrel on September 14.
Festive-season orders are keeping mills running, but output above 80 per cent is in question once seasonal demand cools.

title: India’s textile & apparel exports grow 6.39% in August
content:
India’s textile and apparel exports grew 6.39 per cent YoY to $3.119 billion in August 2026, led by a 13.03 per cent rise in textile shipments, while apparel exports fell 2.74 per cent.
April–August exports slipped 0.24 per cent to $15.077 billion, with apparel down 9.10 per cent and textiles up 6.94 per cent.
Raw cotton and cotton waste imports surged 67.67 per cent YoY in August.

title: US House advances Russia Sanctions Bill, India under 100% tariff risk
content:
The US House has cleared a key procedural hurdle for the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by 214-211, with two Democrats joining Republicans.
The vote allows consideration of Senate amendments to HR 5334 but does not constitute final passage. 
A separate House vote on the sanctions bill is expected Wednesday.

title: The $547 bn fibre reset: Synthetics take 71.7% of demand
content:
Synthetics held 71.7% of 2025 textile-fibre demand, but cotton knits generated $128.3 billion, or 44.5% of classified knit trade.
China’s garment exports fell in 2015-2025, while Bangladesh RMG exports climbed and Vietnam’s H1 2026 growth came from upstream segments.
Future sourcing advantage lies in fibre-flexible systems managing cost, traceability, speed and market access.

title: Bangladesh apparel turns to AI as productivity pressure mounts
content:
Bangladesh’s $38.70 billion apparel export sector faces buyer price pressure as energy, finance and compliance costs rise at home.
Snowtex reports up to 25 per cent productivity gains from IoT-linked monitoring, while Sparrow Group cites 5–10 per cent gains.
EU apparel exports fell 16.43 per cent to €8.64 billion in H1 2026; US exports fell 6.5 per cent in January–July 2026.

title: Switzerland’s OEKO-TEX expands textile traceability in 2025-26
content:
OEKO-TEX expanded traceability across textile supply chains in 2025/26, with ORGANIC COTTON certification present in over 20 countries and certified fibre volume exceeding 33 million kg at ginning level.
Certificates rose by more than 200 per cent, while MADE IN GREEN label demand increased over 13 per cent as regulations tightened globally.

title: BKMEA urges Bangladesh govt to form garment policy panel
content:
BKMEA has urged Bangladesh's government to create a high-level committee to coordinate garment-sector policymaking. 
The proposed body would bring ministries, revenue officials and apparel-textile associations together to address industry issues. 
The agenda covers fair codes, energy planning, stakeholder-led policy changes, transport digitalisation and building-code implementation.
